historical_record.description: Bethany United Methodist Church had dedicated a garden on this site by September 2002.

Fire gutted Trinity United Methodist Church, which then stood on this corner, on 11 October 1981: the roof collapsed, the organ fell into the basement and the stained glass was broken. The fire department called it arson and put the loss at $750,000. The building also housed the Eureka Theatre and an independent congregation, Grace Community Chapel.

In November 2001, twenty years after the fire that destroyed Trinity United Methodist Church at 2299 Market Street, the lot was still vacant behind a chain link fence. Plans to rebuild the church and a proposed four-story AIDS Life Center had both lapsed, and in 2001 the congregation, merged with Bethany United Methodist Church in 1998, was planning a multi-use building.

Bethany United Methodist Church announced a plan for a four-storey ministry center on the vacant lot at 2299 Market Street, costing 10 million dollars and holding two congregations and a child care center; it hoped to move in by December 2004. It dedicated a garden on the lot on 20 July, to be lent to neighbourhood groups in the meantime.
